top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu alone) is the only proposal that names a writer, and on the common criteria it is the strongest case before the committee. From public knowledge and translation, not verified reading of the Romanian, the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid build memory, the body and dream into a recursive, densely patterned prose with a distinctive voice. The effort is sustained at large scale over decades, which supports a claim to formal ambition and imaginative depth. The citation should rest on the major prose, with the poetry named as its lyric root, because the translated poetry and early work are unevenly covered. The attribution is clean: one writer, one language. Open points remain: how much of the Romanian wordplay and rhythm survives translation, and whether Solenoid widens the project or restages the Blinding trilogy. I could not settle either from reputation. I judge the case strong enough to prefer it to no award, and the unanimity of the openings carries no weight in that judgment. P000 is ranked last because I see no literary case for withholding the prize that outweighs the case for this candidate.
recusal_note: No recusal-level connection apparent from the profile. My long engagement with Central Europe (Prague, Vienna, documentary fiction on Nazism and 20th-century trauma) is thematic proximity to a Romanian writer, not a documented personal or professional tie. It may produce a familiarity effect, which I have tried to discount.
